mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when this trigger is met in at least three out of the last five tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE remains below 5% for three consecutive months in at least four out of the last six such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate in at least two of the last three NBER-defined recessions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes, or the mechanism fails in at least three out of the last five manufacturing recessions.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate by more than 1% within a single month signals an emergency monetary easing in response to a financial shock, which boosts liquidity and risk appetite, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such emergency easing episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate in at least one of the last three major financial crises.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month is impossible; however, a sharp drop in PAYEMS while UNRATE remains stable indicates involuntary layoffs, signaling deteriorating labor market conditions and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < -1% AND UNRATE monthly change within [-0.1%, +0.1%]
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes, or the trigger does not precede a NBER-defined recession in at least two of the last three instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% for four consecutive months, combined with a flat or declining personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > +5% for four consecutive months AND GDPC1 monthly change ≤ 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate during at least two of the last three post-crisis balance-sheet repair phases.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.4% for four consecutive months signals an expansion in manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods where INDPRO rises by >0.4% for four consecutive months in at least three out of the last five expansions.
